page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 20 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration consists of 20 physical cores with one thread per core under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.2 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing, as measured by stress-ng, falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15708.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9927.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 69.81 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 29.73 GB/sec for large block write operations. Notably, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds for small language models (135M) at 2344.1 tokens/sec, though text generation and larger model inference remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model offers a resource-dense configuration with a high core count at a lower qualitative price point than dedicated hardware. The primary tradeoff is the potential for CPU steal time or variable single-core performance due to the shared nature of the physical AMD EPYC cores. This server is best suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the 20 cores without requiring sustained, high-frequency single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded file decompression, database operations, and moderate-scale general-purpose application hosting.
